issues.title: The board's `m`/`M` never bounces a `waiting-for-user` card whose stale phase still classifies ClassInProgress - it opens a real /gogo:go launch confirmation instead
issues.description: cli/internal/tui/move.go's attemptActionForce switches purely on f.Class. Its ClassInProgress arm is: `if bounce := m.capBounce(f); bounce != "" && !force { return bounce }; return m.intentFor(launch.ActionGo, f), false, ""` - there is no check anywhere in move.go for f.WaitingForUser() / f.Status == "waiting-for-user". A feature parked at a genuine decision gate (status: waiting-for-user, open-decision: D<n>) classifies ClassInProgress whenever its (necessarily stale, since a gate freezes mid-phase) phase field still names implement/review/test (contract.inProgressPhaseOrStatus matches on PHASE OR status, and phase is untouched by the gate write) - which is the normal, expected shape of a paused decision gate, not a contrived edge case. Verified live: built a scratch fixture (status: waiting-for-user, phase: implement, open-decision: D1) in the unified board. The card correctly shows the '⏸ decision' pill, the gate stripe, and counts in the header's '⏸ K need you' - all of model.go's RENDER-layer logic knows about the gate. But pressing `m` (and, identically, `M`) opens a real huh confirmation: `will run: claude "/gogo:go gate-survives" in tmux session gogo-go-gate-survives ...` - with no bounce, no warning that the card is paused on a decision. Confirmed no equivalent guard exists anywhere in move.go. By contrast, the SAME safety property is already correctly enforced twice elsewhere in this exact codebase: cli/go.go's cmdGo refuses via `!orchestrator.RunnableStatus(f.Status)` (RunnableStatus is false for waiting-for-user), and internal/tui/pickup.go's autoPickupReady explicitly requires `f.Status != "plan-accepted"` to disqualify a gated member from auto-firing. move.go's manual-launch path is the one place this project's own established pattern (a decision gate must be a hard, deterministic launch-guard, never left to the spawned session's own prompt) was not applied. Mitigating factor, verified by reading commands/go.md: the spawned /gogo:go session's very first documented instruction is an 'Acceptance gate' that reads state.md and explicitly says 'waiting-for-user is NOT runnable here... Otherwise STOP' - so a competent session would very likely self-abort rather than silently clobbering anything. But that is prose enforcement, and this whole feature's own thesis (Slice A, D1) is that a safety property must not rest on 'the LLM noticing' - code-review-standards.md check #13 says the same: 'a guard that prevents damage must key on a deterministic signal ... a writer that can skip must be detectable rather than silent.' This is the same class of gap from a different angle: the risk isn't the exit-write clobbering state.md (REV-022, verified fixed and independently mutation-tested this round), it's that the board's OWN launch guard never consults the gate at all, so relaunching a paused decision costs nothing but a keypress and a confirm.
issues.proposed_solution: Add a check to attemptActionForce (move.go), evaluated OUTSIDE the `!force` guards exactly like the FR4/FR4a authoring/plan-unwritten checks (so `M` cannot force past it either): if f.WaitingForUser() (or a direct f.Status == "waiting-for-user" check), return a bounce naming the open decision and its unblock, e.g. "<slug> is paused on a decision (D<n>) - resolve it (see decisions.md) and re-accept first", mirroring cmdGo's runnableHint("waiting-for-user") wording so the two surfaces agree. Add a test alongside TestAttemptActionGuards asserting a ClassInProgress feature with Status: "waiting-for-user" bounces (not launches) for both m and M.
issues.fix_summary:
Reproduced first: a ClassInProgress card at `waiting-for-user` yielded intent `/gogo:go demo` with an EMPTY bounce for both m and M. Fixed in attemptActionForce, before the class switch and OUTSIDE every !force condition - the exact FR4a shape, because a decision gate is a legality rule and `M` overrides the cap "and only that guard". The refusal is decisionGateBounce(f): it names the open decision BY ID when state.md carries one ("demo is paused on D3"), points at decisions.md, and names the legal move (`/gogo:resume demo`), mirroring cmdGo's runnableHint so the two surfaces agree; routed through statusBlocked so it reads blocked, not failed.

INTERACTION WITH REV-022 CHECKED, both directions. TestDecisionGateKeepsItsDisplaySignals pins that a paused card keeps WaitingForInput, its gate stripe, its ⏸ count and its ⏸ card cue - so it is refused AND visibly explains why, rather than being silently unlaunchable. TestDecisionGateIsNotLaunchable's last arm pins the ESCAPE: once the status moves on (what /gogo:resume does), the same card yields ActionGo again. A gate you cannot leave would be worse than one you can bypass, so that is asserted, not assumed.

Mutations: 7 targeted reverts, all caught - removing the check, moving it inside !force (M could relaunch a paused card), moving it after the class switch (unreachable for in-progress cards), dropping the unblock, dropping the decision ID, downgrading the severity, and the two-part form (remove the check AND disable its m/M subtests).

issues.title: TestReviewStandardsDoNotInviteTheExitWriteRemoval's second check is fragile to markdown line-wrapping and can silently miss the exact regression it exists to catch
issues.description: skills_lint_test.go's TestReviewStandardsDoNotInviteTheExitWriteRemoval has two checks on .gogo/knowledge/code-review-standards.md: (1) the file still contains "Do NOT flag the exit write as duplication", and (2) it does NOT contain "write sits after the work rather than" (the old, regression-inviting wording). Reproduced the regression live to verify the guard bites (per the coordinator's explicit request): reintroducing the old wording as ONE WRAPPED markdown line ("...write sits after the work\n    rather than...", the natural shape of an 80-column-wrapped edit) made check (2) a NO-OP - `strings.Contains` does not match across the newline+indentation the wrap introduces, so the file was back to instructing a reviewer to flag the restored exit write as a defect and the test still PASSED. Only when the exact same phrase was kept on one unwrapped physical line did check (2) correctly fail. Check (1) is unaffected by this (it matches a shorter phrase that is unlikely to wrap), so the guard is not fully blind - but its second, more specific assertion (catching the literal old wording) has a real gap for the single most likely way a human edit would reintroduce it.
issues.proposed_solution: Normalize whitespace before the Contains checks in TestReviewStandardsDoNotInviteTheExitWriteRemoval - e.g. `strings.Join(strings.Fields(body), " ")` (collapses all runs of whitespace/newlines to single spaces) before testing for "write sits after the work rather than", so a natural line-wrap of the forbidden phrase still matches. Add a test case that reintroduces the phrase pre-wrapped across two lines and asserts the guard still fails.
issues.fix_summary:
Normalised whitespace before matching - `strings.Join(strings.Fields(body), " ")` - so the phrase match survives a natural markdown re-wrap. Verified with a CONTROL PAIR rather than a single mutation, because a guard-hardening revert cannot fail while the defect is absent: with the forbidden phrase reintroduced WRAPPED across a line break, the hardened guard fails (1) and the raw-matching guard passes (0). That is the proof the normalisation is load-bearing. Both files restored byte-for-byte, md5-verified, matching the tester's own discipline.

Worth recording: my first attempt at this verification used an anchor written from MEMORY of the file's line wrapping; it did not match, the edit never landed, and the run reported 0 failures - a false pass that the landed-edit check caught. That is the same class as the nameless-CAUGHT rule and is why both are in the harness.

issues.title: A raw templates/state.template.md scaffold renders a bogus `⛓ ×3` correlation chip from misparsed legend prose
issues.description: cli/internal/contract/state.go's parseStateFile scans state.md line-by-line and matches ANY line of the shape `- **key:** value` via the stateLine regex, with no tracking of whether that line sits inside a still-open multi-line `<!-- ... -->` block. stripComment only strips a trailing SAME-LINE comment opener (`strings.Index(s, "<!--")` on that one line); it does nothing for a comment that began on an earlier line and closes on a later one. templates/state.template.md's own optional-correlation legend (lines ~39-41, wrapped in one multi-line HTML comment) carries an EXAMPLE line: `- **correlation:** [plan-XXXX]   plan id(s) this item belongs to, e.g. [plan-7f3a, plan-9c2e]`. That example line independently matches stateLine, so parseStateFile treats it as a REAL correlation field, and parseCorrelationList splits its prose on commas into 3 bogus plan ids (`plan-XXXX]   plan id(s) this item belongs to`, ` e.g. [plan-7f3a`, ` plan-9c2e`). Any work item scaffolded directly from templates/state.template.md with the legend intact - which is exactly this plan's own prescribed Slice-A hands-on fixture ('scaffold a work item from templates/state.template.md with NO plan.md') - therefore renders a false `⛓ ×3` chip claiming membership in 3 cross-source plans it does not belong to. Verified live in the tmux-driven unified board: at full pane width the chip expands to the three literal bogus ids (`⛓ plan-XXXX]   plan id(s) this item belongs to ⛓ e.g. [plan-7f3a ⛓ plan-9c2e`), which is direct visual proof of the exact misparse. This is a pre-existing gap in parseStateFile/stripComment (predates 0.29.0 - the correlation field and its legend comment shipped earlier), not something this plan's changes introduced, but it sits in the same function this plan's FR6 (stripPlaceholder) extends, and it is triggered by precisely the fixture shape this plan's own test scenarios call for.
issues.proposed_solution: Make parseStateFile comment-aware across line boundaries instead of per-line: track an 'inside an unclosed <!--' boolean as the scanner walks lines (open on a line containing <!-- with no matching --> later on that same line; close on the line carrying the matching -->), and skip stateLine matching entirely while that flag is set. Alternatively/additionally, strip the whole leading legend block (from the file's first <!-- to its closing -->) before line-scanning begins. Either keeps stripComment's existing trailing-same-line-comment behaviour for genuine inline comments unchanged, and only closes the multi-line gap.
issues.fix_summary:
Fixed with a block-aware parse, as specified. parseStateFile now carries an 'inside an unclosed <!--' flag across lines (contract.advanceComment) and skips any line that STARTS inside a comment, so a `- **key:**` line that exists only as example prose inside a legend block is no longer a field. Single-line behaviour is byte-for-byte: `<!--` and `-->` on one line leave the flag false, the line still parses, and stripComment still trims the trailing comment from the value. Edge cases decided and documented in the doc comment, all in the 'may only ever make a value MISSING, never wrong' direction: a stray `-->` with nothing open is ignored; a line that closes a comment and then carries a key is treated as commented (a shape no template or real state.md uses); and an UNTERMINATED `<!--` comments out the rest of the file - deliberately, because that is what every markdown renderer shows the user - which is not silent, since the keys after it go missing and the card reads as malformed/authoring rather than plausibly wrong. Keys BEFORE the opener still parse, so a truncated write loses only what follows it (pinned by test).

GUARDS, structural as suggested: TestShippedTemplateScaffoldParsesClean and (at the render layer) TestTemplateScaffoldRendersNoCorrelationChip read templates/state.template.md ITSELF, not a copy, so the guard cannot drift from what ships; both first assert the template still CONTAINS the commented-out example, so they cannot pass because the hazard was removed instead of handled. The card must carry no `⛓`, the real keys must still parse, and a genuine `correlation:` line outside any comment must still yield exactly its ids. Plus TestAdvanceCommentEdges (11 boundary shapes) and TestParseStateFileCommentBlocks (6 parse-level cases).

THE GUARD PAID FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY. My first draft of the template's new warning note contained a literal `-->`, which closed the legend block early and reopened this exact defect - the template-reading test failed on the spot. The note is now phrased without comment tokens, and both the template and advanceComment's doc record that a closer appearing in prose inside a block ends it, exactly as a markdown renderer would: that is what the file MEANS, not a parser bug to work around.

Verified live on the plan's own prescribed fixture (a scaffold copied verbatim from the shipped template, no plan.md): `gogo status` reads it cleanly, and the board card shows `✎ authoring` with NO chip at 200 and at 400 columns - the width at which the tester saw the three literal bogus ids. 12 revert mutations, compile-checked with nameless-CAUGHT-unscored and two-part guard mutations, all caught; one of them (reading the carry-in flag AFTER advancing instead of before) found a real coverage gap - a key line whose trailing comment OPENS a multi-line block - which is now its own test case.
